sourcedFrom: PORQ CHOP & SHORT CHOP BY Q — OWNER'S MANUAL — © 2021 (2021)
cleanIntro: The Short Chop is an 8.6 mm stainless can on Q's Quickie XL fast-attach mount — 7.2 inches, 9.6 oz. It rides a CHERRY BOMB XL muzzle brake, not the barrel threads. ⚠ Q shares one book between the PORQ CHOP and the SHORT CHOP and the procedure really is identical; what differs is length and weight, which is why they are two rows and one procedure. Centrefire rifle rules apply: the taper is the job, the bath is optional.

steps.title: Magazine out, action open, chamber checked by eye AND by hand
steps.action: Before any maintenance: magazine out of the host, action open, and the chamber and magazine well confirmed empty by a PHYSICAL and a VISUAL inspection. Q asks for both, in that order, and both is the point — a look into a dark chamber is one check, not two.
steps.prose: This is the first line of Q's maintenance section, not a preamble to it.
steps.quote: BEFORE PERFORMING ANY MAINTENANCE ON YOUR FIREARM, REMOVE THE MAGAZINE FROM YOUR FIREARM
steps.cite: PORQ CHOP & SHORT CHOP BY Q — OWNER'S MANUAL — © 2021 — Cherry Bomb Installation — safety block, p.1
steps.warn: AS WITH ALL FIREARMS CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, ALWAYS WEAR PROPER PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT SUCH AS GLOVES AND SAFETY GLASSES.

steps.title: ⛔ 8.6 mm (.338 in) or smaller — that is the whole rating
steps.action: Confirm the projectile diameter and the ammunition before you handle the can. Short Chop: Q states the bore limit on the cover of its own book, and states separately that only factory certified SAAMI / C.I.P. ammunition goes through it.
steps.prose: A bore limit and an ammunition standard are two different constraints and Q prints them as two lines.
steps.quote: THE PORQ CHOP & SHORT CHOP SILENCER IS FOR USE WITH 8.6 MM OR SMALLER PROJECTILES.
steps.cite: PORQ CHOP & SHORT CHOP BY Q — OWNER'S MANUAL — © 2021 — Warnings block, p.1
steps.warn: ONLY USE FACTORY CERTIFIED SAAMI / C.I.P. AMMUNITION WITH THIS SILENCER.

steps.title: Silencer off — counter-clockwise, and let it cool first
steps.action: Clear the host again if it has been out of your hands. Then unthread the silencer counter-clockwise off the Cherry Bomb. ⚠ Q's own advice is to wait before touching it if you have just been shooting — a centrefire can comes off the rifle hot enough to burn through a glove.
steps.prose: It threads onto the brake, not onto the barrel. What comes off is the can; the brake stays where it is.
steps.quote: Torque clockwise onto the Cherry Bomb to 10-15 lbs.
steps.cite: PORQ CHOP & SHORT CHOP BY Q — OWNER'S MANUAL — © 2021 — Silencer Installation, step 2, p.2

steps.title: ⚠ A centrefire rifle can is NOT cleaned like a rimfire or pistol can
steps.action: Q says this outright, and it governs everything below: a centrefire rifle silencer does not need the cleaning cycle a rimfire or a pistol can needs. There is no schedule here and no round count — there is a taper to keep clean and an optional bath.
steps.prose: If you came to this from a .22 can, unlearn the routine. Over-cleaning this one costs you more than leaving it alone.
steps.quote: CONTRARY TO WHAT THE INTERNET SAYS, A CENTERFIRE RIFLE SILENCER DOES NOT REQUIRE THE SAME CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE AS A RIMFIRE OR CENTERFIRE PISTOL SILENCER.
steps.cite: PORQ CHOP & SHORT CHOP BY Q — OWNER'S MANUAL — © 2021 — Cleaning & Maintenance, p.2

steps.title: The taper and threads — this is the part that actually matters
steps.action: Clean the Cherry Bomb's taper and threads, and the matching features inside the silencer, of any fouling. Q's stated reason is alignment: a clean taper is what keeps the can concentric to the bore axis. ⛔ No steel tools — solvent-moistened Scotch-Brite, or a brass or nylon brush.
steps.prose: Everything else on this can is optional. This is the step that decides whether the bullet goes down the middle.
steps.quote: Clean the CHERRY BOMB’s taper and threads as well as the corresponding silencer features of any fouling. This will help with alignment of the silencer to the barrel’s axis, ensuring optimal performance.
steps.cite: PORQ CHOP & SHORT CHOP BY Q — OWNER'S MANUAL — © 2021 — Cleaning & Maintenance, step 1, p.2
steps.warn: DO NOT USE STEEL TOOLS FOR CLEANING. WE RECOMMEND USING A PIECE OF SOLVENT MOISTENED SCOTCH-BRITE™ OR A BRASS OR NYLON BRUSH.

steps.title: Internals: a copper-solvent or ultrasonic BATH, then drain it fully
steps.action: If you want the internals clean, Q's method is submersion — a copper solvent or an ultrasonic cleaner. ⛔ When it comes out, rinse it and make sure the can is FULLY DRAINED before use. Solvent trapped in a baffle stack goes down the bore on the next shot.
steps.prose: "If you wish" is Q's word. This is an option on a centrefire can, not a duty.
steps.aside: When removed from it’s bath, rinse and make sure the silencer is fully drained before use.
steps.quote: If you wish to clean internals of the silencer, we recommend submerging it in a copper solvent or an ultra sonic cleaner.
steps.cite: PORQ CHOP & SHORT CHOP BY Q — OWNER'S MANUAL — © 2021 — Cleaning & Maintenance, step 2, p.2

steps.title: Back on the brake — clockwise, 1.25 inch SAE flats on the rear
steps.action: Thread the silencer clockwise onto the Cherry Bomb and torque it to 10-15 lbs using the rear wrench flats. ⛔ NO thread locker between the silencer and the Cherry Bomb — that joint is meant to come apart.
steps.prose: The Rocksett belongs on the barrel threads under the brake, and nowhere else on this assembly.
steps.quote: The PORQ CHOP & SHORT CHOP silencers features 1.25 in SAE wrench ﬂats on the rear. We recommend you use these for install and removal.
steps.cite: PORQ CHOP & SHORT CHOP BY Q — OWNER'S MANUAL — © 2021 — Silencer Installation, step 1, p.2

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Never thread the Cherry Bomb into the silencer first
deepSteps.action: The brake goes onto the BARREL first and the silencer goes onto the brake second. Q states the failure mode plainly: thread the Cherry Bomb into the silencer before it is on a barrel and it will get stuck.
deepSteps.prose: It is the one assembly-order mistake this system allows, and it is not recoverable at the bench.
deepSteps.quote: DO NOT THREAD THE CHERRY BOMB INTO THE SILENCER BEFORE IT IS PROPERLY INSTALLED ONTO A BARREL. IT WILL GET STUCK.
deepSteps.cite: PORQ CHOP & SHORT CHOP BY Q — OWNER'S MANUAL — © 2021 — Cherry Bomb Installation — safety block, p.1

deepSteps.title: Cherry Bomb onto the barrel — degrease, Rocksett, then torque
deepSteps.action: Take any existing muzzle device off. Clean and degrease the muzzle threads with solvent, apply Rocksett to the barrel threads, and thread the brake on clockwise. A 9/16 inch SAE socket, to Q's printed spec — and on a tapered shoulder Q skips the Rocksett step entirely. ⛔ No washers, no shims, no jam nuts — the Cherry Bomb needs no timing and they only misalign it.
deepSteps.prose: This joint is semi-permanent by design. Get the thread pitch right the first time.
deepSteps.quote: Right tighty. Using a 9/16 inch SAE socket, tighten the CHERRY BOMB XL according to the below specs.
deepSteps.cite: PORQ CHOP & SHORT CHOP BY Q — OWNER'S MANUAL — © 2021 — Cherry Bomb Installation, step 4, p.1
deepSteps.warn: THEY CAN CAUSE MISALIGNMENT AND THE CHERRY BOMB DOES NOT REQUIRE TIMING.

deepSteps.title: 24 hours before live fire — the Rocksett has to cure
deepSteps.action: Q asks for a 24-hour cure on the Rocksett for best results. That makes brake installation a day-before job, not a morning-of one.
deepSteps.prose: Firing on uncured thread locker is how a brake walks loose and takes the silencer's alignment with it.
deepSteps.quote: 5.Allow Rocksett to cure for 24 hours for best results.
deepSteps.cite: PORQ CHOP & SHORT CHOP BY Q — OWNER'S MANUAL — © 2021 — Cherry Bomb Installation, step 5, p.1

cleaning.name: TAPER AND THREADS — THE REAL JOB
tasks: Cherry Bomb XL taper and threads cleaned of fouling
The silencer's matching features cleaned to match
⛔ No steel tools — Scotch-Brite or a brass/nylon brush only

cleaning.name: INTERNALS — OPTIONAL
tasks: Copper solvent or ultrasonic bath if you want it
Rinsed, then ⛔ FULLY DRAINED before use

cleaning.name: BEFORE IT GOES BACK ON
tasks: 1.25 inch SAE rear flats used for install and removal
10-15 lbs clockwise onto the Cherry Bomb XL
⛔ No thread locker on the silencer-to-brake joint

reassembly: Cherry Bomb XL on the barrel first — never threaded into the silencer off the gun.
Correct Cherry Bomb for your thread: M18-1.5, 3/4-24 or 5/8-24.
Silencer clockwise onto the brake, 10-15 lbs, on the 1.25 inch rear flats.
No thread locker between silencer and brake.
fncheck: Confirm the can is fully seated on the Cherry Bomb XL, that nothing rotates or wobbles, and that the bore is clear and dry. Check the projectile against the 8.6 mm (.338 in) limit and that the ammunition is factory SAAMI / C.I.P. If the brake was installed today with Rocksett, it has not cured — that is a 24-hour wait, not a range trip.
